dimension_resolution.output: kt_id_set (small flat_array of int32, expect 2 ids)

filters.notes: ~4 of 134k keywords; per-row inside CSR range

filters.predicate: info_type_id == it1_id AND info IN country_set
note NOT LIKE '%(USA)%' AND note LIKE '%(200%)%'

join_order.build: title (filtered: production_year>2005 AND kind_id in kt_id_set)
join_order.probe: movie_keyword via primary CSR on movie_id
join_order.notes: Driver scan over title; CSR probe gives contiguous rows; semi-join exit on first row whose keyword_id is in k_id_set

join_order.probe: movie_info via primary CSR on movie_id
join_order.notes: Per candidate movie_id, iterate CSR range; require info_type_id==it1_id AND info in country_set; early-exit on first match

join_order.probe: movie_info_idx via primary CSR on movie_id
join_order.notes: Per candidate, iterate CSR range; require info_type_id==it2_id AND info<'8.5'; keep all matches because we need MIN(mi_idx.info) over surviving rows

join_order.build: company_name (pre-scanned: country_code != '[us]' → bitset by row, plus pos[id]→row valid filter)
join_order.probe: movie_companies via primary CSR on movie_id
join_order.notes: Pre-scan company_name once: build bitset[N_cn] for country_code != '[us]'. For each candidate movie_id, iterate mc CSR range; apply note filters; map company_id → cn row via company_name__id__pos; test bitset; keep all surviving rows for MIN(cn.name)

data_structures.country_set: std::unordered_set<std::string_view> with 10 country literals for mi.info test
data_structures.cn_country_ok_bitset: std::vector<uint8_t> size N_company_name (~235k bytes) — pre-scan once
data_structures.fact_probes: primary CSR offsets (mmap) — no hash tables built

parallelism.notes: Per-thread local MIN(cn.name), MIN(mi_idx.info), MIN(t.title); merge at end with lexicographic min

indexes.purpose: literal id lookup (optional; resolution via direct scan)

execution_outline: 1. mmap all needed columns and indexes.
2. Resolve scalar/set ids: it1_id, it2_id, kt_id_set, k_id_set (linear scan of small dimension text columns).
4. Build country_set unordered_set<string_view> for mi.info membership test.
5. Parallel morsel scan over title rows r in [0, N_title):
b. Skip if title.kind_id[r] not in kt_id_set.
d. SEMI on movie_keyword: iterate CSR [mk_off[tid], mk_off[tid+1]); break-on-match where mk.keyword_id in k_id_set. If none, skip.
e. SEMI on movie_info: iterate CSR [mi_off[tid], mi_off[tid+1]); break-on-match where mi.info_type_id==it1_id && mi.info in country_set. If none, skip.

f. Walk movie_companies CSR [mc_off[tid], mc_off[tid+1]); for each row apply note LIKE '%(200%)%' AND NOT LIKE '%(USA)%'; lookup cn_row=company_name_pos[mc.company_id]; require cn_row>=0 && cn_country_ok_bitset[cn_row]; collect candidate mc rows (and cn_row).
g. If no surviving mc rows, skip.
h. Walk movie_info_idx CSR [midx_off[tid], midx_off[tid+1]); for each row require info_type_id==it2_id && info<'8.5'; collect surviving midx rows.
i. If no surviving midx rows, skip.

j. For each (surviving mc row, surviving midx row) -- conceptually cartesian within tid -- update thread-local mins: cn.name via company_name.name[cn_row], mi_idx.info via mi_idx.info[midx_row], title via title.title[r]. Since aggregates are MIN only, we just need min over distinct surviving rows: update min(cn.name) over surviving cn_rows, min(mi_idx.info) over surviving midx rows, min(t.title) once per surviving tid (guarded by both sides non-empty).
6. Reduce per-thread mins into final triple.
aggregation: scalar_min_triple (no group by) — per-thread local MIN buffers reduced at end; early-exit NOT safe (lex min needs full scan of survivors)
